subject: literature
passage: Mrs. Halloran had long prided herself on receiving bad news as she received the post: promptly, and without remark. When her brother's letter arrived announcing that the old family house at Kilrush was to be sold, she read it once at the breakfast table, folded it along its original creases, and asked the maid whether the bread had come. Only later, when she found herself in the garden at an hour she never went there, standing before the gooseberry bushes she had grown from cuttings taken at that very house, did she understand that she had been composing, all morning, a reply she had no intention of sending.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Mrs. Halloran is secretly relieved that the old family house at Kilrush is finally to be sold.
choices.B: Mrs. Halloran resents her brother for deciding to sell the house without asking her.
choices.C: Mrs. Halloran's calm response to the news hides, even from herself, how much it affects her.
choices.D: Mrs. Halloran's lifelong composure finally gives way when she breaks down in the garden.

explanation.why: Two parts of the text must be read together. At breakfast she reacts "without remark," folding the letter and asking about the bread. Later, standing by bushes grown from the house's cuttings, she realizes she has been "composing, all morning, a reply." The words "Only later ... did she understand" show that her calm surface hid her feelings even from her own awareness.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Her drift to the gooseberry bushes from the old house and her mental reply suggest she is unsettled by the sale, not relieved.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says the brother failed to consult her, and it does not reveal what her unsent reply says.
explanation.C: Correct. Her outward calm at breakfast contrasts with her later realization; "only later ... did she understand" shows the feeling was hidden even from her.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This overstates the garden scene: she quietly realizes something, but nothing suggests she breaks down.

checks.note: Best fit on the text alone.
